children: Google plans to invest at least 13 billion euros ($15 billion) in artificial intelligence infrastructure in Finland over the next two years.

The investments across four locations, planned between 2027 and 2028, include the construction of data centers and supporting infrastructure, in addition to support for clean energy projects and dedicated nature and community funds.
"This is Google's largest single investment in Europe," it said in a statement.

"The new digital infrastructure will serve as building blocks for Finnish and broader European digital readiness, innovation, and AI development, and will power Google's popular services — such as Gemini, Search, Maps, and YouTube."
As part of its digital infrastructure build-out in the country, Google said it is also allocating funds to new energy capacity, grid enhancements and energy affordability initiatives.

It has signed power purchase agreements with domestic onshore wind power providers and contracted a new battery system to connect to Finland's grid to help with grid balancing and stabilizing electricity prices.

Google currently has a data center in Hamina, on Finland's south coast. The site is a former paper mill that it bought in 2009 and converted. The financing announced Wednesday includes fresh investments at the site and three other locations spread throughout the country.
